## Load packages

`pacman` loads the required packages and installs any that are missing. `here::i_am()` places
this notebook in the repository, so paths resolve from the repository root. `enrichVolcano`, the
user's own plotting package (not on CRAN), is called with `::`.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, tidyr, purrr, stringr, ggplot2, readxl, writexl)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/03_enrich_scatter_fgsea/a_script/03_enrich_scatter_fgsea.qmd")
```

## Read set tests

Do both modalities move the same biology? This step sets each gene set's fgsea NES in BFR
training against its NES in HLRT training. NES, the normalised enrichment score, is positive when
a set's members sit towards the top of the protein ranking and negative towards the bottom. No
new test is run; everything comes from `set_tests` in `01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx`.

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "03_enrich_scatter_fgsea")
set_tests <- read_excel(
  here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry", "c_data", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx"),
  "set_tests"
)
count(set_tests, method)
```

## Pair the two contrasts

Keep fgsea rows for the two training contrasts and widen to one row per set, with `_x` columns
for BFR_Post-Pre and `_y` for HLRT_Post-Pre. `significance` records which arm reaches BH 0.05.
A set is discordant when its two NES sit on opposite sides of zero; each discordant set here is
significant in one arm only, so the opposite sign rests on the other arm's null. `survivor` marks
sets that survived `collapsePathways` in either arm.

```{r pair}
x_contrast <- "BFR_Post-Pre"
y_contrast <- "HLRT_Post-Pre"
paired <- set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", contrast %in% c(x_contrast, y_contrast)) |>
  mutate(contrast = if_else(contrast == x_contrast, "x", "y")) |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(set_id, database, pathway, n),
    names_from = contrast, values_from = c(NES, padj, main)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      padj_x < 0.05 & padj_y < 0.05 ~ "Both",
      padj_x < 0.05 ~ x_contrast,
      padj_y < 0.05 ~ y_contrast,
      .default = "NS"
    ) |> factor(c("Both", x_contrast, y_contrast, "NS")),
    discordant = sign(NES_x) != sign(NES_y),
    survivor = main_x | main_y,
    label = enrichVolcano::clean_label(pathway)
  )
head(select(paired, set_id, NES_x, NES_y, significance, discordant), 4)
count(paired, significance)
```

## Concordance

`concordance()` takes a paired table and returns one row: sets, significant sets, discordant
significant sets, Spearman's rho between the two NES with its p, and the share of significant
sets with the same sign in both arms. The warning about ties in `cor.test()` is suppressed; the
p-value is then approximate.

```{r concordance-helper}
concordance <- function(data) {
  test <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(data$NES_x, data$NES_y, method = "spearman"))
  hits <- filter(data, significance != "NS")
  tibble(
    sets = nrow(data), significant = nrow(hits), discordant = sum(hits$discordant),
    rho = round(unname(test$estimate), 3), p = test$p.value,
    same_sign = round(mean(!hits$discordant), 3)
  )
}
```

Three populations: every set, the collapse survivors, and Hallmark with GO Slim. Hallmark and GO
Slim do not nest, so no branch of the GO:BP hierarchy weights rho towards its largest branch.

```{r populations}
survivors <- filter(paired, survivor)
curated <- filter(paired, database %in% c("Hallmark", "GO_Slim"))
```

## Figure

`as_enrichment()` turns the fgsea rows into `enrichVolcano`'s enrichment object, and
`plot_scatter()` draws the two contrasts' NES against each other for Hallmark and GO Slim.

```{r figure}
enrichment <- set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", contrast %in% c(x_contrast, y_contrast)) |>
  transmute(contrast, database, pathway, NES, pval = p, padj, size = n, leadingEdge) |>
  enrichVolcano::as_enrichment(enrichment_test = "fgsea")
figure <- enrichVolcano::plot_scatter(
  enrichment, x_contrast, y_contrast,
  databases = c("Hallmark", "GO_Slim"), collapse = FALSE,
  theme = enrichVolcano::plot_theme(base_size = 9, base_family = "sans")
) +
  labs(
    title = "Hallmark and GO Slim",
    caption = str_wrap(paste(
      "S10 Figure. NES concordance, Hallmark and GO Slim.",
      sprintf(
        "fgsea NES for the %d Hallmark and GO Slim sets in %s (x) against %s (y).",
        nrow(curated), x_contrast, y_contrast
      ),
      "These two collections do not nest, so no branch of the GO:BP hierarchy weights rho.",
      "Grey sets reach neither threshold; coloured ones are significant (BH < 0.05 within",
      "contrast) in one or both. Shaded quadrants move the same way in both contrasts, with",
      "their counts in the corners; dashed line is identity. The subtitle gives Spearman's rho.",
      "Data: nes_scatter sheet of 03_enrich_scatter_fgsea.xlsx."
    ), 100)
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, lineheight = 1.2),
    plot.caption.position = "plot"
  )
```

S10 goes to `b_reports/03_enrich_scatter_fgsea_figures.pdf`.

```{r write-figure}
pdf(
  file.path(stage, "b_reports", "03_enrich_scatter_fgsea_figures.pdf"),
  width = 8.27, height = 11.69
)
print(figure)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Concordance summary

One row per population.

```{r summary}
summary_table <- list(
  "all collections" = paired, "collapse survivors" = survivors, "Hallmark and GO Slim" = curated
) |>
  map(concordance) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "population")
summary_table
```

## Save results

`03_enrich_scatter_fgsea.xlsx` holds the concordance table, the discordant significant sets, and
both NES with adjusted p for every set, rounded for reading.

```{r write}
export <- paired |>
  transmute(
    set_id, database, pathway, label,
    genes = n,
    nes_x = round(NES_x, 3), nes_y = round(NES_y, 3),
    padj_x = signif(padj_x, 4), padj_y = signif(padj_y, 4),
    significance = as.character(significance), discordant, survivor
  ) |>
  arrange(significance, desc(abs(nes_x) + abs(nes_y)))
sheets <- list(
  concordance = summary_table,
  discordant = filter(export, discordant, significance != "NS"),
  nes_scatter = export
)
overview <- data.frame(
  sheet = names(sheets), rows = map_int(sheets, nrow), columns = map_int(sheets, ncol),
  description = c(
    "NES agreement between training contrasts",
    "Sets with opposite NES signs",
    "NES and adjusted p, both contrasts"
  )
)
write_xlsx(
  c(list(overview = overview), sheets),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "03_enrich_scatter_fgsea.xlsx")
)
```
